<docs>
Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about the harness itself, its SDK, extensions, themes, skills, or TUI):
- Main documentation: /usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/README.md
- Additional docs: /usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs
- Examples: /usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples (extensions, custom tools, SDK)
- When reading pi docs or examples, resolve docs/... under Additional docs and examples/... under Examples, not the current working directory
- When asked about: extensions (docs/extensions.md, examples/extensions/), themes (docs/themes.md), skills (docs/skills.md), prompt templates (docs/prompt-templates.md), TUI components (docs/tui.md), keybindings (docs/keybindings.md), SDK integrations (docs/sdk.md), custom providers (docs/custom-provider.md), adding models (docs/models.md), packages (docs/packages.md), environment variables (docs/environment-variables.md), MCP servers (docs/mcp.md), codemode scripts and non-LLM models such as classifiers and image models (docs/codemode.md)
- Before implementing harness changes, read the relevant docs and examples in full, following related cross-references.
</docs>
sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents
- mcp: Use mcp to connect to Streamable HTTP servers, discover tool schemas, and call their tools.

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>

toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.
toolsAdded.name: read

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.
toolsAdded.name: bash

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.
toolsAdded.name: edit

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.
toolsAdded.name: write

content.description: Content to write to the file

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

toolsAdded.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.
toolsAdded.name: grep

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

toolsAdded.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).
toolsAdded.name: find

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

toolsAdded.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).
toolsAdded.name: ls

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

toolsAdded.description: Connect to an unauthenticated Streamable HTTP MCP server and use its tools. Use action=list without server to see configured servers; action=connect with server and url to connect; action=list with server to inspect its discovered tool schemas; action=call with server, tool, and arguments to invoke a tool. HTTP/HTTPS only; no stdio, OAuth, or custom authentication headers. Connections are private to this session.
toolsAdded.name: mcp

Arbitrum One supports two different types of USDC : Native USDC : USDC tokens that are native to the Arbitrum One chain. Bridged USDC ( USDC.e ) : Ethereum-native USDC tokens that have been bridged to Arbitrum One. Differences between USDC and USDC.e Copy Anchor Link Native USDC Bridged USDC Token Name USDC Bridged USDC Token Symbol USDC USDC.e Token Address 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 0xff970a61a04b1ca14834a43f5de4533ebddb5cc8 Benefits CEX Support, directly redeemable 1:1 for U.S. dollars The Arbitrum Bridge will continue to facilitate transfers of all USDC tokens. When depositing Ethereum-native USDC , the option exists to receive Bridged USDC using Arbitrum's bridge (the canonical lock-and-mint flow described in the token bridging deep dive ) or Arbitrum-native USDC using Circle's Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol . To start bridging on Arbitrum refer to the Quickstart or the Embedded bridge widget . If you run into issues bridging USDC , see Arbitrum bridge: Troubleshooting . For Arbitrum chain operators Copy Anchor Link If you're launching an Arbitrum chain and want to support USDC without locking users into the canonical bridged form, see How to adopt the bridged USDC standard on your Arbitrum chain . It explains the gateway implementation that lets Circle upgrade your chain's USDC to native issuance later. Historical context Copy Anchor Link The Arbitrum Bridge will continue to facilitate transfers of all USDC tokens. When depositing USDC from Ethereum, the option exists to receive USDC using Circle's Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol or receive Bridged USDC using Arbitrum's lock-and-mint bridge. In 2023, Circle launched USDC natively on Arbitrum One and added support for the Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol, which enabled direct minting and burning of USDC between Ethereum and Arbitrum One. Due to this, the token symbol for Bridged USDC has been renamed to USDC.e to accommodate an ecosystem-wide liquidity migration to native USDC . The expectation is that over time, the liquidity migration of USDC.e to USDC will continue. OpenChainBench probes each endpoint every minute from three regions. It publishes the p50, p95, and p99 latency under an open methodology and the CC BY 4.0 license. Sequencer endpoint behavior Copy Anchor Link Arbitrum One has two public endpoints with different roles. The public RPC URL is for general use. The direct sequencer endpoint accepts only eth_sendRawTransaction and eth_sendRawTransactionConditional . The table compares their purpose and operational guarantees. The two endpoints at a glance Copy Anchor Link Endpoint Purpose Operational guarantees https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc (public RPC URL) General-purpose read/write endpoint, useful for development and low-volume reads. No uptime, latency, or rate-limit guarantees. If your decentralized app depends on availability, use a third-party node provider or run your own node. https://arb1-sequencer.arbitrum.io/rpc (sequencer endpoint) Direct submission path to the chain's sequencer for write traffic. Accepts only eth_sendRawTransaction and eth_sendRawTransactionConditional . Has the queueing and timeout behavior described below. It is still a best-effort public endpoint with no formal service-level agreement (SLA). Latency and timeout behavior Copy Anchor Link Under normal load, the sequencer endpoint accepts a transaction in less than a second. The sequencer puts each submission in a bounded in-memory queue. By default, the queue holds 1,024 transactions. The queue timeout is 12 seconds by default. It limits how long a transaction can wait in the queue before the sequencer picks it up or rejects it. The timeout is not an end-to-end inclusion latency guarantee. If the sequencer does not pick up the transaction before the timeout, eth_sendRawTransaction returns context deadline exceeded . In that case, the sequencer did not accept the transaction, and you can safely retry it. Recommended fallback patterns Copy Anchor Link Use a third-party node provider as your primary endpoint, or as a fallback when a direct sequencer submission fails. Retry only on transient errors. You can safely retry context deadline exceeded and network or connection errors with backoff. Do not retry terminal errors, such as nonce too low or contract reverts. The response does not mean that the transaction is posted in a batch to the parent chain , or final there. If your app needs parent-chain finality, track it separately. content.text:
The production and staging network configurations in `config.json` have been migrated from Ethereum to Arbitrum One and Arbitrum Sepolia:

- **Network Identities & RPC/Explorer Endpoints**:
  - **Production (Arbitrum One)**: Set chain ID to `42161`, name to `Arbitrum One`, RPC endpoint to `https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc`, and explorer URL to `https://arbiscan.io`.
  - **Staging (Arbitrum Sepolia)**: Set chain ID to `421614`, name to `Arbitrum Sepolia`, RPC endpoint to `https://sepolia-rollup.arbitrum.io/rpc`, and explorer URL to `https://sepolia.arbiscan.io`.
- **Sequencer Routing & Submission Policy (`rpcPolicy`)**:
  - Configured dedicated sequencer submission endpoints (`https://arb1-sequencer.arbitrum.io/rpc` for production, `https://sepolia-rollup-sequencer.arbitrum.io/rpc` for staging).
  - Set `sequencerSubmissionOnly` to `true` and restricted `sequencerAcceptedMethods` to `["eth_sendRawTransaction", "eth_sendRawTransactionConditional"]`.
  - Configured `retryableSubmissionErrors` to handle transient `context deadline exceeded` errors and `terminalSubmissionErrors` to include `execution reverted` and `nonce too low`.
- **Withdrawal Finality & Force Inclusion (`finalityPolicy`)**:
  - Set `withdrawalsToEthereumAreInstant` to `false` for both networks.
  - Set `challengeWindowBlocks` to `45818` (Arbitrum One dispute window) and `20` (Arbitrum Sepolia dispute window).
  - Set `forceIncludePeriodBlocks` to `7200` (Arbitrum One delayed inbox limit) and `5760` (Arbitrum Sepolia delayed inbox limit).
- **Canonical Bridge Onboarding (`assetOnboarding`)**:
  - Set `preferredRoute` to `canonicalBridge` and enabled `canonicalBridge.enabled` on both networks.
- **Token Identities (`tokens`)**:
  - **Arbitrum One**: WETH (`0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1`), native USDC (`0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831`), and bridged `USDC.e` (`0xff970a61a04b1ca14834a43f5de4533ebddb5cc8`).
  - **Arbitrum Sepolia**: WETH (`0x980B62Da83eFf3D4576C647993b0c1D7faf17c73`), native testnet USDC (`0x75faf114eafb1BDbe2F0316DF893fd58CE46AA4d`), and `USDC.e` kept `null`.
- Preserved application settings (`application`, `wallet`, `retry`, `contracts.multicall3`, etc.) and configuration structure.
